decisions.reason: As a close-to-core design variant in a growing market, it likely stays because its modest incremental cost and fit with the firm's aesthetic-service positioning give management enough slack to wait for demand to settle.

This shower channel is tightly aligned with the firm's established drainage business and barrier-free bathroom trend, so even if early sales are mixed it is still likely to be retained while management learns from the launch.

Because the pump-assisted solution is more technically complex and niche than the firm's standard offer, it faces the highest risk of falling short of aspirations, but current slack and its strategic relevance make continued market presence more likely than withdrawal.

A tileable floor drain with grating is a very natural extension of the firm's core range, so boundedly rational management would usually keep it unless early results were clearly well below aspiration.
This stainless steel design grate complements the existing portfolio and can be carried at relatively low organisational cost, which supports keeping it while the firm broadens its design-led offer.
